## Recruitment process overview:

Capgemini conducts on-campus and off-campus recruitment, and the company targets students from various disciplines, offering them flexibility. The recruitment process consists of several stages, and each stage assesses different skill and competency sets.

## Round 1: Written English Test and Technical Assessment

In this round will check your Grammar, vocabulary, or technical sense check \* Sentence correction \* Prepositions \* Grammar \* Reading comprehension \* Synonyms & Antonyms \* Speech and Tenses \* Article usage \* Spotting Errors \* Sentence arrangement As well as the ability to check data structures, algorithms, DSA, fundamentals of the database, cloud, and networking.

## Round 2: Coding Assessment

In this round, the candidates eligible for higher package roles will be subjected to a coding assessment round. This round is mandatory and shall assess the coding skills and algorithmic problem-solving skills.

## Round 3 : Spoken English Assessment

In this round Spoken English would be a new round introduced for evaluating the spoken English proficiency of all candidates. The sections in the assessment include grammar and reading comprehension, listening, and speaking.

I recently appeared for the Cognizant GenC technical interview, and I wanted to share my experience to help others preparing for it.

The interview was mostly technical, with a small HR touch at the end. The interviewer was calm and gave enough time to think and answer.

- Can we create an object of an abstract class?

- Difference between method overloading and overriding

- What is encapsulation and why is it used?

👉 They were more interested in concept clarity rather than very deep internals.

No complex queries were asked.

title: CRED Mark: Values and Beliefs
reported: Managerial 'CRED Mark' round with an engineering lead about your values, internships, competitive programming journey, personal projects and how CRED works.

sources.passage:
me a lot to ace this interview. I didn’t needed to specifically prepare for this round.   
The round started with discussion of the approach that I used in Round-1 and scope of improvement in it. Then there were similar functions we needed to implement in this round which were as follows.   
**a.** How do we handle concurrency and multithreading. You need to be clear with basic understading of DBMS such as ACID/CAP properties and basics of threading.  
**b.** Many problems involving data-structures knowledge and clear algorithmic approaches.

There were few more functions which I don’t remember now but were pretty intersting to have a discussion on them. Only 4 people were selected for the next round.

**Round 3: CRED Mark**This is kind of managerial discussion where you are connected with a Engineering Team Lead at CRED. This conversation would be centered around you and they would like to know and learn more about you — your behaviors and values & belief system that has shaped you. It was a very good discussion round and lasted for an hour.   
This round started with our introductions. The interviwer was very friendly. It started with a long discussion of my internship at Goldman Sachs. He dived into the project that I was working on and my experience so far in the internships such as difficulties that I faced, how I built an understanding of the current project and many stuff related to that.   
Then we started discussion of my background in college and had a discussion on my Competitive Programming journey. After this we had a discussion on my personal projects like the

CRED. there were 4 language options: python, node.js, java, and c++. i chose python as i am comfortable with it. the initial functions were to do some basic crud operations. if you have a good grip on the concepts of OOPs and the programming language, you should be comfortable with it. i completed the project in around 60 minutes and focused the rest of the time on making the code more readable and clean. this round ended at around 2:30 pm.

i was initially sceptical about whether i could get this opportunity, but when the results were out, i got to know that there was a good enough chance for me to win.

**the third round**

the interview round started at around 4:30 pm. the first interview was purely technical and was focused more on the fundamentals. the interviewer asked some questions regarding extending the project from the second round and what algorithms we could use to attain them.

most of the questions were to determine how clear our fundamentals were and how we could modify an existing algorithm to fit our needs. the interview was for 90 minutes.

we waited for some 60–90 minutes for the results. meanwhile, we were handed out some cool CRED merchandise :)

**the final round**

the results were out, and it came down to the last 3. the next round of interviews started at around 8 pm and lasted for 60 minutes. this round was managerial and was with the head of engineering (backend). they asked me about what i did in my 3 years at IIT. most of the time went in talking about my past internships and projects; then, there were a few questions regarding how CRED works,

title: Implement a Skeleton Class
reported: Given a class skeleton with empty methods, design the data structures and implement the logic with clean, extensible code; be comfortable with method chaining (obj.foo().bar()).

sources.passage:
crucial to thoroughly understand the role you’re applying for, especially after receiving a referral. For example, expressing interest in AI and ML while applying for an infrastructure position may not align well with the recruiter’s expectations.

After this, I was scheduled for a 1-hour phone screen, where I was asked a typical Databricks medium-level question. The interview went smoothly, and the next day, I received a link to schedule a virtual onsite interview.

The onsite interview consisted of four parts:

1. Algorithm Interview: This was similar to the phone screen(LC medium) but involved two interviewers.
2. Cross-Functional Interview: A typical behavioral interview where I discussed my experiences.
3. System Design Interview: This involved designing a simple system, discussing scalability, trade-offs, and other considerations.
4. Coding Interview: The goal here was to design a class and implement it while working with the interviewer. I struggled with this part, mainly because I hadn’t found many references or resources to prepare effectively.


A few days later, I received a rejection. The first three interviews are managable, but the last one was challenging due to the limited reference material available for preparation. But my advice for the coding round is, know your language very well - classes, objects, funciton chaining implementation(your_object.foo().bar()). 

Let me know if you have a question, but couldn't share specifics because of the NDA.

**UPDATE** : Looking back on the 4th round, The questions looks like Amazon's OOD/LLD questions.
